data.name: Rishabh
data.gender_notes: Rishabh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who rules over the universe, the embodiment of the cosmic order and dharma, the first son of God Indra and the god of agriculture and wealth. The name Rishabh carries the meaning “Master, Ruler, Lord” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Rishabh usually hope their child will grow to embody master, ruler, lord and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the divine power that governs the universe, symbolizes the first son of a deity and the embodiment of dharma and order.
data.etymology: Rishabh belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Master, Ruler, Lord.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rishabh total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Rishabh" is of significant cultural importance in Hindu mythology, representing the first son of the God Indra and the prince of Himavat - the king of mountains. Rishabh is also revered as the God of Agriculture, patron of livestock, and the source of the Vedic tradition.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Rishabh" holds deep spiritual significance in the Hindu tradition, symbolizing the cosmic order and dharma that rules the universe. The sound of the name is believed to purify the mind and inspire a sense of devotion and harmony with the divine force. In deep meditation, the name "Rishabh" can help transcend the boundaries of earthly consciousness, connecting one to the universal and eternal truth.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Rishabh is a Sanskrit name meaning 'first' or 'foremost'. It is believed to be the name of the first ruler of the world, the progenitor of the Ikshvaku dynasty, and the embodiment of dharma (righteousness) and stability.

historical_references.reference: Rishabh is considered as the first Tirthankar or Jain prophet in Jainism. According to the Jain scriptures, Rishabh was the first being to attain kaivalya or omniscience, and thus, he is considered as the Adi Tirthankar or the first Tirthankar.
historical_references.context: Jainism is an ancient Indian religion that follows the teachings of 24 Tirthankars, who are considered as spiritual teachers and saviors. Rishabh is considered the first among these Tirthankars.

historical_references.reference: Rishabh is also known as Vibhishana in Hindu mythology, who was the younger brother of King Ravana of Lanka. He is considered to be a faithful and noble advisor to Ravana and a strong devotee of Lord Vishnu. During the war between Rama and Ravana, Vibhishana defected from his brother's side and joined Rama's army, after which he was blessed by Lord Vishnu and given the kingdom of Alaka in the southern part of India.
historical_references.context: Hindu mythology has various characters and stories, and Rishabh, also known as Vibhishana, is one of them. He is known for his loyalty and devotion to Lord Vishnu.

modern_usage.modern_context: In the modern world, the name 'Rishabh' is often associated with individuals who are making a mark in technology, entrepreneurship, and innovation. Rishabhs can be found leading tech startups as Founders or CTOs on platforms like LinkedIn and AngelList. They are also known to write insightful articles on engineering and innovation on Medium, showcasing their expertise and thought leadership in their respective fields.
